title: Exponential size bound for tree-unrolling
statement: Let $F$ be a Boolean feedforward circuit from the inputs $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ to an output type, in which every gate has finitely many input wires, and suppose $k \in \bbn$ bounds these arities, so that each gate has at most $k$ input wires. Then for every layer $m \le \mathrm{depth}(F)$ and every node $v$ of layer $m$, the tree-unrolling of $v$ is a Boolean circuit of size at most $(k+1)^m$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean feedforward circuit F with inputs Fin n
k bounds every gate's arity (at most k input wires)
m is a layer index (m < depth + 1)
v is a node of layer m
replaced:
If every gate of $F$ has at most $k$ input wires, i.e.\
$\mathrm{card}\,(F.\texttt{gates}\ d\ v).\texttt{op}.\iota \le k$ for all $d$ and $v$,
then the unrolling of any node at layer $m$ has size at most $(k+1)^m$.
